detail.head:
Subjective

The patient reports breathing is easier.

Objective

Vital signs: not dictated today.

Physical examination not documented in today's dictation.

Testing Results

Chest X-ray Oct 9: bilateral pleural effusions.

TTE Oct 10: EF 30%.

Renal ultrasound: pending.

Assessment

Patient is a 74-year-old man with a history of chronic kidney disease stage 3 and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction who presented with volume overload on Oct 9. He has been receiving intravenous diuretic therapy during this admission. Today he reports improved dyspnea, suggesting response to ongoing diuresis. Renal function and volume status remain the focus of management.

Plan

1. Continue intravenous furosemide for acute on chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; monitor clinical response to diuresis.

2. Chronic kidney disease stage 3 — trend creatinine daily.

3. Renal ultrasound — pending; obtain result and review findings.
